learningObjective: Interpret MLIR gpu.launch_func: grid/block dimensions, memory-space conventions, kernel argument passing, and per-thread indexing.

canonicalClaims.claim: MLIR `gpu.launch_func` separates `blocks in (...)` and `threads in (...)` clauses so that total threads = product of block-count and threads-per-block; kernel arguments include memref types; per-thread global index typically requires `blockIdx * blockDim + threadIdx`, not `blockIdx + threadIdx`.
nonImplications: Does not imply memory-space integers are portable across targets.
Does not imply `gpu.launch` (inline-region form) is deprecated.

misconceptions.claim: Total thread count is only the `blocks in` product.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Total threads = blocks × threads-per-block; both are honored by lowering.

misconceptions.claim: Memory space 1 in gpu memref denotes shared memory.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Standard convention: 0 = global (default), 3 = workgroup/shared, 5 = private on NVVM lowering.
Memref args are the primary way to pass tensor data; they are lowered to base pointer + descriptors.

misconceptions.claim: `gpu.block_id x` returns the global thread index including intra-block position.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It returns only the block coordinate; global index needs `block_id * blockDim + thread_id`.

implementationFacts: `gpu.func ... kernel` marks a device entry point.
